newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark protests interconnect draft.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark protests interconnect draft.

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark A/S said on Monday it had protested to the government about draft legislation on interconnection deals for competitors' access to its network under deregulation.
"In its draft the government is proposing competitors' access fees to Tele Danmark's network below bottom level long-run incremental costs," Tele Danmark told Reuters.

"This is much lower than European Union fee stipulations and would hit Tele Danmark hard, causing us major losses. It could have the most serious economic consequences for Tele Danmark of all the liberalisation measures so far," the spokesman said.
He said Tele Danmark's chairman Knud Heinesen and deputy chairman Nils Wilhjelm wrote a protest letter to Danish research minister Jytte Hilden on February 20.
The Danish teleconmmunications sector was deregulated on July 1, 1996 and the second phase enabling legislation is due to be processed by parliament next month.
